sections.markdown:
## C2 - Confusables and KG hints, Section Two Signals

FACT_ID: sec02-R01 | anchor: A01
Right on red is allowed from any street after a stop, while left on red is allowed only from a one-way street onto another one-way street [A01].
Why it matters: group signal-meanings; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec02-F04, sec02-F06 [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-R02 | anchor: A01
A steady red arrow holds you stopped with Virginia banning the turn, while a flashing red arrow releases you after a stop and yield when clear [A01].
Why it matters: group signal-meanings; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec02-F07, sec02-F10 [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-R03 | anchor: A01
A steady yellow orders a stop from outside the intersection, while a flashing yellow orders only slower, cautious travel [A01].
Why it matters: group signal-meanings; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec02-F11, sec02-F12 [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-R04 | anchor: A01
Flashing red demands a full stop plus a yield before going, while flashing yellow demands no stop at all [A01].
Why it matters: group signal-meanings; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec02-F09, sec02-F12 [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-R05 | anchor: A01
A steady red light holds you stopped for its whole phase, while a flashing red light lets you proceed once stopped, yielded, and clear [A01].
Why it matters: group signal-meanings; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec02-F03, sec02-F09 [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-R06 | anchor: A02
A red X bans its lane entirely, a yellow X orders a safe exit from the lane, and a green arrow opens the lane [A02].
Why it matters: group lane-signals; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec02-F16, sec02-F17, sec02-F18 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec02-R07 | anchor: A02
Turning on a plain green light without an arrow means yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, while a green arrow in your direction means going when clear [A02].
Why it matters: group signal-meanings; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec02-F14 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec02-R08 | anchor: A02
Solid double reds on a pedestrian beacon hold drivers stopped with walkers crossing, while the later alternating flashing reds release drivers with caution once the crosswalk clears [A02].
Why it matters: group lane-signals; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec02-F19 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec02-R09 | anchor: A02
The eight-sided octagon always commands a full stop, while the triangle commands only slowing with a stop as needed [A02].
Why it matters: group sign-language; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec02-F23, sec02-F24 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec02-R10 | anchor: A02
Black with white states a law to obey, yellow with black warns of a hazard, and red with white orders stop, yield, or no [A02].
Why it matters: group sign-language; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec02-F21 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec02-R11 | anchor: A02
Orange with black warns through construction zones, while pink with black warns at incidents [A02].
Why it matters: group sign-language; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec02-F22 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0008]
